description: This case study is the summarized English version of the final report of the Investigation Committee on the major blackout caused by the 2018 Hokkaido Eastern Iburi Earthquake, published by OCCTO on 19 December 2018 (36 pages of slides). It sets out the sequence of events from the earthquake to the blackout and from the blackout to a secure supply capacity of about 3,000 MW, the finding that the loss of three Tomato-atsuma units and four transmission lines combined with a saturated Hokkaido-Honshu HVDC link caused frequency collapse, and the black start, which took about 45 hours to restore almost the whole area. It lists short-term measures for winter 2018/19 such as 350 MW of under-frequency load shedding and revised relay settings, and notes that the committee found no issue in the operation or system structure of Hokkaido Electric Power Company. Access: free PDF from OCCTO; no licence is stated. Coverage is one island grid. Caveats: this is the summary deck and only its first pages were read; the household count comes from search summaries. It suits cascading failure and resilience studies of island grids with frequency control limits, and it relates to the OCCTO information service catalogued here as data-occto-power-system-information.

name: Final Report on the Major Blackout caused by the 2018 Hokkaido Eastern Iburi Earthquake (OCCTO investigation committee, December 2018)
outcomes: The committee found the blackout resulted from composite factors: shutdown of Units 1, 2 and 4 of the Tomato-atsuma thermal plant and of hydro plants after four transmission lines, including the Karikachi trunk line, were lost. Emergency power transfer over the Hokkaido-Honshu HVDC link reached its maximum, so frequency control could not act when Unit 1 tripped. Restoring almost the entire area took about 45 hours, and short-term measures for winter 2018/19 include 350 MW of extra under-frequency load shedding and adjusted operation of the Tomato-atsuma and Kyogoku units. Search summaries give about 2.95 million households without power.
